text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000152 bills 99215 well above the risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, but records cover too few claims to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The complexity breakdown cuts against a pure sicker-panel explanation: the 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider share in each condition-count band, including 0- and 1-condition patients. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s on diagnoses that typically support simpler visits, such as follow-up (Z09), rash (R21) and urinary tract infection (N39.0), for example C0077700, C0079571 and C0079740. However, most 99215s still fall on patients with 2 or more conditions, and the overall mix leans heavily toward 99214, which may reflect a consistently high-billing style or a genuinely complex practice. The documentation is too thin to judge: records cover well under 1% of claims, with a single documented 99215 (C0079732, supported). The notes showing moderate-or-higher data reviewed all had a lab or test line on the claim, so there is no cloning signal either way. A reviewer should first request a targeted sample of charts for 99215 claims on 0–1 condition patients, starting with the sampled claim IDs above, and check whether the documented MDM and time support the billed level."}
